html:
Amman became the capital of Transjordan in 1921, when it was a small town. It is now a city of about four million people.

It is an ancient place: Rabbath Ammon, capital of the Ammonites, and the Roman city of Philadelphia, whose theatre still stands in the centre. After centuries of decline, it was resettled in 1878 by Circassians, Muslim refugees from the Russian conquest of the Caucasus.

Each wave of refugees made it grow: Palestinians in 1948 and 1967, Iraqis after 1991 and 2003, and Syrians after 2011. It spreads across many hills, with the old Citadel at its heart. See also the Amman Message and Circassian exodus.
sum: Amman became the capital of Transjordan in 1921, when it was a small town. It is now a city of about four million people.
